status: fixed before V11 fitting; exploratory after V1 final results and V2-V10 development results were viewed
question: Do longer SRT price-return horizons reveal a stable signal before adding analyst-motivated information or fuzzy state interactions?
target_asset: SRT.SI raw closing price, not the iEdge index level
forecast_time: after SRT close on trading day t
existing_five_day_reference: V2-H7; do not relabel its failed original-input Ridge screen as a new discovery
inner_selection: last 15 percent of eligible outer training windows; fit-label end must precede first inner-stop forecast; choose lowest inner-stop RMSE, larger alpha on exact tie; refit on all eligible outer training windows
evaluation_boundary: evaluation label ends no later than 2025-09-30; outer fit labels end strictly before first evaluation forecast; never inspect or rank on the previously viewed final_holdout
advance_rule: For each horizon separately, Ridge pooled RMSE at least 1 percent below the best of the three simple baselines, better in at least two of three folds, and pooled MAE no more than 1 percent worse than that baseline. This is a development screening heuristic, not independent confirmation.
interpretation: Overlapping horizon labels reduce effective independent evidence; metrics must not be compared numerically across horizons. The 60-day result is descriptive with this short SRT history, even if it passes the heuristic.
next_phases_not_yet_authorized_as_result: Mechanism: same-horizon, same-date simple-model ablations for published rates, point-in-time valuation, and DPU/debt information; no present-day fundamentals backfilled into history
State: only after an information group passes screening, predefine a small number of rate-by-volatility or rate-by-debt interactions and match non-fuzzy controls
Any changed primary horizon or architecture must be disclosed as a revised course proposal before replacing the approved experiment
